Japan.residency: resident only if your domicile is in Japan or you've lived there a year; 90-day visa-free visits stay non-resident.

USA.residency: 183-day test weighted over 3 years: coming every year, 122+ days/yr makes you resident (121 is safe). Closer-connection exception (Form 8840) can protect you up to 182 days. ESTA visitors max 90 days per visit; longer needs a B-2 visa.
USA.income_note: 37% federal + state (MA 9% over $1M, UT 4.65%); worldwide income. US citizens pay this wherever they live.

home_rule.note: a home in Canada is a significant residential tie: with weak ties elsewhere CRA can treat you as resident (worldwide income taxed) even under 183 days. A vacation home with strong ties abroad usually stays non-resident, but it's a real risk.

home_rule.note: any home you can use makes you resident. Second-home rule: if your centre of life has been abroad 5+ yrs, using the Austrian home on no more than 70 days a year keeps you non-resident (keep a day log).

home_rule.note: a home kept as your habitual residence can make you resident under 183 days.

Portugal.income_note: 48% + 5% solidarity; 28% flat on investment income. IFICI ('NHR 2.0'): 20% on qualifying jobs and most foreign income exempt for 10 yrs, if you qualify.
Portugal.property_note: IMT ~6% + 0.8% stamp duty; IMI 0.3-0.45% + AIMI above €600k

Malaysia.residency: 182 days, or shorter stays linked to longer ones across years.
Malaysia.income_note: foreign income brought in by individuals is exempt until end-2036.
Malaysia.property_note: foreigners pay 4% flat stamp duty; some states add a foreign levy (e.g. Penang 3%); RM1M+ minimum price for foreigners in most states

Thailand.income_note: since 2024, foreign income is taxed if brought into Thailand (not if kept abroad). LTR-visa holders: foreign income exempt.
Thailand.property_note: transfer fee 2% (often split); foreigners cannot own land: condo or 30-yr lease only

Chile.residency: 183 days in any 12 months (or across 2 consecutive years).
Chile.income_note: foreigners pay only on Chilean income for their first 3 years, then worldwide.
Chile.property_note: notary + registry; contribuciones ~1% of fiscal value (rural land often exempt)

home_rule.note: centre of vital interests in Poland makes you resident.

Poland.income_note: 32% + 4% solidarity above PLN 1M; 19% on capital income; 19% flat option for business income.
Poland.property_note: 2% PCC on resale; property tax per m², very low; farmland restricted for non-farmers

home_rule.note: centre of vital interests in Romania makes you resident.

Romania.income_note: 10% flat income tax (plus health contributions); dividends 16%.
Romania.property_note: notary + registration; building tax ~0.1-0.2%/yr; non-EU buyers cannot own land directly

Brazil.residency: 183 days in 12 months; a permanent visa makes you resident from day one.
Brazil.income_note: 27.5% on salary; 15% on offshore investments since 2024; new minimum tax on high earners from 2026.
Brazil.property_note: ITBI 2-3% + registry; IPTU/ITR; limits on foreign ownership of rural land

Indonesia.income_note: worldwide; skilled expats can elect Indonesian-income-only for the first 4 years.
Indonesia.property_note: BPHTB 5% + notary; foreigners only via Hak Pakai (right-of-use) or company

home_rule.note: a 'permanent place of abode' in NZ makes you resident whatever the days. IRD (IS 25/16): a holiday home used 2-3 months a year isn't one by itself, but ownership counts toward your ties and courts have found ownership alone enough. Investor-visa home buyers are being told to get a binding ruling.

New Zealand.residency: 183 days in any 12 months, or a permanent place of abode.
New Zealand.income_note: new residents: most foreign income exempt for the first 4 years; no capital-gains tax.
New Zealand.property_note: no stamp duty or capital-gains tax (2-yr bright-line on homes); FOREIGNERS CANNOT BUY HOMES except Australians/Singaporeans or Active Investor Plus visa holders (one home worth NZ$5M+, law passed Dec 2025); rural/sensitive land needs Overseas Investment Office consent

Argentina.residency: resident after 12 months or with permanent residency.
Argentina.income_note: worldwide; plus an annual wealth tax (bienes personales).
Argentina.property_note: provincial stamp tax + deed costs; rural land limits for foreigners

home_rule.note: settling (domicile) in Turkey makes you resident.
domicile with intent to stay makes you resident; a holiday home alone usually doesn't.

Switzerland.residency: 90 days without work (30 days if working).
Switzerland.income_note: varies a lot by canton (Zug ~22%, Zurich ~40%); non-working foreigners can negotiate lump-sum (forfait) taxation in many cantons.
Switzerland.property_note: cantonal transfer tax + notary; wealth + property tax; Lex Koller caps holiday-home sales to foreigners

home_rule.note: domicile in Fiji (your permanent home) makes you resident.

Fiji.residency: 183 days in any 12 months, or domicile.
Fiji.income_note: residents: 0% to FJD 30k, 18-20% to FJD 270k, then 33-39% (39% above FJD 1M); non-residents 20% from the first dollar. Dividends untaxed since 2017; 10% CGT on gains, for residents also on foreign assets. Workers on contracts of up to 3 yrs: foreign income exempt.
Fiji.property_note: stamp duty abolished Aug 2020 (legal/registration costs only); 10% capital gains tax when you sell; foreigners can't buy residential land inside town boundaries and must build (FJD 250k+) on vacant residential land within 2 yrs; 12.5% VAT on some sales

Georgia.income_note: 20% flat; foreign income exempt (territorial); 1% turnover tax for small businesses.
Georgia.property_note: flat registration fee; property tax 0-1% only above an income threshold; foreigners cannot buy farmland

home_rule.note: your 'foyer' (main home) there makes you resident.

New Caledonia.income_note: rough: own territorial income tax, top ~40%.

Vanuatu.property_note: rough: leasehold only (75-yr leases); stamp duty + lease registration; no income or property tax

Grenada.property_note: Alien Landholding Licence 10% of value for foreigners; buyer stamp duty ~1%

home_rule.note: a permanent place of abode in Australia makes you resident.

Australia.income_note: 45% + 2% Medicare; temporary-visa residents don't pay on foreign income.
Australia.property_note: stamp duty + 8-9% foreign surcharge; land-tax foreign surcharge 2-5%/yr; ban on foreigners buying established homes 2025-27

home_rule.note: Statutory Residence Test: a home available to you plus 90+ days the year before = 2 ties, so returning visitors become resident from 121 days.

United Kingdom.income_note: Scotland 48% top rate; new arrivals: foreign income and gains exempt for the first 4 years (FIG regime).
United Kingdom.property_note: Scotland: LBTT up to 12% (~10% effective at £2M) + 8% ADS if you own another home anywhere (reclaimable if it becomes your main home); council tax

home_rule.note: your 'foyer' (main home/family) or main work in France makes you resident; a holiday home alone doesn't.

France.income_note: 45% + 4% high-income surcharge; ~30% flat on investment income; impatriate regime for workers moving in.
France.property_note: notary + registration ~7.5-8% on resale; taxe foncière; IFI wealth tax above €1.3M

home_rule.note: 'ordinarily resident' if SA is your real home.

South Africa.income_note: worldwide; dividends 20%, capital gains effectively up to ~18%.
South Africa.property_note: transfer duty up to 13% above ~R12M; municipal rates; register foreign funds with the Reserve Bank to repatriate later

home_rule.note: your habitual abode or centre of interests in Italy makes you resident.

Italy.income_note: 26% on investment income. New residents can pay a flat €200k/yr on ALL foreign income for 15 yrs; 7% flat for foreign pensioners in small southern towns.
Italy.property_note: 9% registration tax on a second-home resale (on cadastral value); IMU on second homes

home_rule.note: centre of economic interests or family in Spain makes you resident.

Spain.income_note: savings income 19-30%. Beckham law: 24% on Spanish work income, foreign income exempt, for 6 yrs. Regional wealth tax.
Spain.property_note: ITP 6-10% by region on resale; IBI; regional wealth tax

home_rule.note: permanent home/centre of vital interests in Greece makes you resident.

Greece.income_note: non-dom option: flat €100k/yr on all foreign income (needs €500k investment); 7% flat for foreign pensioners; half-tax for relocating workers.

home_rule.note: owning or renting a home you use (domicile) can make you resident.

Croatia.income_note: top rate 30-33% depending on city; 12% on capital income.
Croatia.property_note: 3% transfer tax; holiday-home property tax since 2025

home_rule.note: 60-day rule: with a Cyprus home, a local job/company and no other tax residence you can choose to be resident after 60 days (then non-dom: 0% on dividends).

Cyprus.income_note: non-dom residents: 0% on dividends and interest for 17 years; foreign pensions 5%.
Cyprus.property_note: land-registry transfer fees 3-8% (halved on resale without VAT); no annual property tax; non-EU buyers need a permit

home_rule.note: intention to live in Malta makes you resident.

Malta.income_note: non-domiciled residents pay nothing on foreign income they keep abroad (minimum €5k tax).
Malta.property_note: 5% stamp duty; no property tax; non-EU buyers need an AIP permit outside special designated areas

home_rule.note: 90 days + a permanent home + UAE residence visa or job gets you a UAE tax-residence certificate.

UAE.property_note: Dubai Land Department 4%; no property tax

Panama.property_note: 2% transfer tax; property tax 0.5-1% above exemptions

home_rule.note: setting up your home (casa habitación) in Mexico makes you resident; with homes in two countries your centre of vital interests decides.

Mexico.residency: no fixed day count; 183 is a rule of thumb.
Mexico.property_note: acquisition tax 2-4%; within 50 km of the coast foreigners buy through a bank trust (fideicomiso)

home_rule.note: buy property worth ~US$430k+ and stay 60 days: you can become tax-resident (and use the 11-year holiday).

Uruguay.income_note: 12% on foreign dividends/interest, but new residents get an 11-year holiday on foreign investment income.
Uruguay.property_note: 2% transfer tax + fees; contribución inmobiliaria; small wealth tax

Philippines.income_note: resident foreigners are taxed only on Philippine income.
Philippines.property_note: documentary stamp + transfer + registration; foreigners cannot own land (condos only)

home_rule.note: a registered residence or a rented home on a 183+ day lease makes you resident.

Vietnam.property_note: 0.5% registration fee; foreigners cannot own land, apartments on 50-year terms

Sri Lanka.property_note: 4% stamp duty; foreigners cannot own land freehold (leases up to 99 yrs)

Mauritius.residency: 183 days in a year OR 270 over 3 years: coming every year, 90+ days/yr makes you resident.

Mauritius.property_note: 5% registration duty; foreigners buy through approved schemes (IRS/PDS/smart city)

Bahamas.property_note: 10% VAT/stamp on transfers (often split); real-property tax up to 1%

Norway.residency: 183 days in 12 months OR 270 in 36: coming every year, 90+ days/yr makes you resident.
Norway.income_note: dividends ~37.8%; wealth tax ~1% on net assets.
Norway.property_note: 2.5% document duty; municipal property tax; wealth tax ~1%

home_rule.note: keeping an 'essential connection' (e.g. a home) to Sweden can keep you resident.

Sweden.income_note: 30% on capital income; expert relief for some workers.

Ireland.residency: 183 days in a year OR 280 over 2 years: coming every year, 140+ days/yr makes you resident.
Ireland.income_note: 40% + USC + PRSI. Non-domiciled residents pay nothing on foreign income kept abroad (remittance basis).

home_rule.note: habitual residence / centre of interests in Slovenia makes you resident.

home_rule.note: your 'foyer' in Morocco makes you resident.
